title: El chofer
goal: Sit up front and get a driver talking for forty minutes
culture: The seat beside the driver is not off limits and it is cooler. Four questions is all it takes; after that your part is listening, and you will learn more Spanish in forty minutes of it than in a week of anything else.

beats.es: Súbase adelante si quiere, joven. Ahí va más fresco.
beats.objective: Ask how long he has been driving
beats.en: How many years have you been driving?
beats.good: Manejar is to drive; conducir is what a textbook says and nobody here. Ask a driver his years and you have bought yourself the whole journey.

beats.es: Veintidós años. Toda la ruta me la sé de memoria.
beats.good: De memoria again — the same phrase the poet used about Darío. He means every curve, every tope and every place the police stand.

beats.es: Toda. Y me gusta, fíjese. No lo cambio.
beats.objective: Ask whether he really likes it
beats.good: Me gusta from him, le gusta from you. He said it first and unprompted, which in a job like his is worth noticing out loud.

beats.es: Cansa, eso sí. Pero uno se acostumbra.
beats.objective: Agree the way he means it
beats.en: You get used to it. That’s right.
beats.good: Uno for I, which turns it into something general — it is how people here say the hard part out loud without it counting as a complaint.
